title: Aligot
subtitle: The stretchy mashed potato of the Aubrac plateau
excerpt: Potatoes beaten with butter, cream, garlic, and melting cheese until the mixture pulls into long ribbons. A dish from the Aveyron that is rich beyond reason and utterly satisfying.
sourceNotes: Traditional Auvergne dish from the Aubrac plateau, Aveyron. Classic combination of tomme fraiche, potato, cream, and garlic.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Aligot does not keep well. Make it just before serving.

content.text: Aligot is a hot, stretchy potato dish beaten with cheese until it pulls into long ribbons. It comes from the Aubrac hills and needs high heat and constant stirring. Work it vigorously or the cheese will clump rather than stretch.
Cover the potatoes with cold salted water. Bring to a boil and cook for 20 minutes until completely tender.
Drain the potatoes well. Return them to the dry pan over low heat for 2 minutes to drive off excess steam.
Mash the potatoes until very smooth. A ricer gives the best texture here.
Add the butter and garlic paste. Beat them in over low heat with a wooden spoon.
Pour in the warm cream. Stir vigorously until fully absorbed and the potato is smooth and glossy.
Add the mozzarella and cheddar a handful at a time. Beat hard after each addition. Keep the heat low and constant.
Keep stirring until the mixture stretches in long ribbons when lifted with the spoon. Season with salt and white pepper. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: The cheese clumps and does not stretch.
items.cause: The potato was not hot enough when the cheese went in.
items.fix: Keep the pan on low heat throughout. Add the cheese in small amounts and beat fast.

items.symptom: The mixture is stiff and stodgy.
items.cause: Not enough cream was added, or the potato variety was too waxy.
items.fix: Stir in a splash more warm cream and beat hard. Use a floury potato next time.

items.cause: It cooled and the starch set.
items.fix: Return it to low heat with a splash of cream and beat to loosen. Serve at once.
